WHY NOT ACCEPTED

1. The automatic production pass is not reachable from any shipped composition. `manager.sweep` discovers the seam with `getattr(operations, "recovery_verification", None)`, but nothing in the product ever sets that attribute. `delegation.ManagerOperations` declares `__slots__` containing `recovery_analysis` and NOT `recovery_verification`, with `object` as its only base, so the attribute cannot even be assigned: I checked, and `o.recovery_verification = seam` raises "no attribute ... and no __dict__ for setting new attributes". `tools/stage_execution.py` binds `self.recovery_analysis = None` in `StageExecution.__init__` and composes a real `RecoveryAnalysis` from the install configuration's `analysis_worker` key (that is how Stage 1-A was made reachable), but there is no analogous binding, no configuration key for the declared execution context or workspace root, and no call to `tools.recovery_execution.verification_seam` anywhere outside the new test module. `tools/job_manager.py` exposes only `recovery-item` and `recovery-decide`; no CLI verb drives `advance_verification` either. Consequence: on a bootstrapped instance running the shipped serve loop, an owner-approved recovery would be admitted and then never materialize, execute or hand off, and the review gate would stay closed indefinitely. `manager._verify` is dead code in every deployment. This is not disclosed as a limitation; manager.py's own docstring states the pass is "called from `manager.sweep` on every tick of every deployment that configures a verification seam, and from `manager.reconcile` on every resume" (reconcile does not call it at all), and REPORT.md presents the seam as "the seam a deployment composes" without saying that no shipped composition does. The joined acceptance proves read, decide, bind/admit, serving and review, but drives the three middle acts by calling `advance_verification` directly in-process, so it does not cover this. Please either wire the seam into the shipped deployment composition (with a case equivalent to the accepted `test_stage_execution` coverage of `composed.recovery_analysis`), or state plainly in the dossier that the runtime driver is deliberately left for a later outcome, and correct the docstring and REPORT wording accordingly.

2. An interior fault cut inside `execute` wedges the loop and reports a false reason. `execute` performs two separate durable writes: its own `recovery.verification-executed` journal transact, then `retained_recovery.record_verification`. Nothing reconciles a crash between them: `execution_readiness` derives `verification` only from `retained_recovery.verification_of`, so with the result committed and the account missing it returns state `unknown`, `owed: None`, and the pass goes silent forever. I reproduced this against the delivered fixture by making `record_verification` raise after the result committed: result journalled `passed`, Stage 1-B account `None`, readiness `unknown / owed None / review blocked`, three further ticks produced zero acts, child-process count 1, gate closed. `record_verification` has exactly one caller and no resume path, so the only way out is owner intervention. The behaviour is conservative (no second process, no inferred success, no released review), but the reported detail says "journalled the intent to run its approved verification and journalled no account of it; whether that command ran is UNKNOWN", which is factually wrong in that state -- the pass's own account exists and says `passed` -- and it contradicts REPORT.md's claim that "a restart at each cut resumes at the next act". A readiness that also consults `execution_result_of`, plus completing the missing account on re-entry, would close this.

3. Dossier evidence inaccuracies. REPORT.md limitation 6 states that "two authority bounded-text cases fail identically on the pinned base", which is contradicted by its own retained authority.log (Ran 511 tests, OK) and by COUNTS.md (authority: 511 collected, 511 passed, 0 failures, 0 errors); my own authority run was also 511 OK. PROGRESS.md says "six cases fail identically on the pinned base" in one paragraph and "the same four results the pinned base produces" in another; the retained baseline/candidate logs show four (three test_tool/test_store_readonly path-message failures plus one test_native_permission error), with identical ids on both sides as claimed. Separately, the focused-acceptance table in COUNTS.md is malformed: its header declares nine columns (including Failed/Errored/Skipped, unittest time, measured wall and Log) but every row supplies module, class and five numbers, so the per-run totals, measured durations and log references the task asks to be retained are absent from that table and survive only as prose in PROGRESS.md.

Minor note, not a blocker: the new test module mutates process-global `os.environ` at import time (`setdefault("BATON_V12_STACK_TEST_ROOT", ...)` after applying the accepted chooser's two rules). It is honestly documented in REPORT.md limitation 7 and uses setdefault so an operator's choice wins, and I confirmed it does not change tests.job_manager.test_fresh_attempt's outcome either way here; but it does decide a suite-global for whatever else shares the process, which is worth the owner's attention since the stated bounded test-change scope is none.

Items 1 and 3 are evidence/claim corrections or a small amount of wiring; item 2 is a narrow reconciliation fix. The rest of the slice -- the five acts, custody immutability, context binding, the gate correction, K M1-M3, the renewed-failure and hold endings, review-only reuse, the replay/restart/concurrency fences and the no-verdict guarantees -- is in good shape and independently verified above.
